claim: Inhibition of type I PRMTs with MS023 increases the proliferative capacity of ex vivo cultured MuSCs.
source: Herein, we show that inhibition of type I protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) with MS023 increases the proliferative capacity of ex vivo cultured MuSCs.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Single cell RNA sequencing of ex vivo cultured MuSCs revealed the emergence of subpopulations in MS023-treated cells which are defined by elevated Pax7 expression and markers of MuSC quiescence.
source: Single cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq) of ex vivo cultured MuSCs revealed the emergence of subpopulations in MS023-treated cells which are defined by elevated Pax7 expression and markers of MuSC quiescence, both features of enhanced self-renewal.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by scRNAseq data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: MS023-specific subpopulations are metabolically altered with upregulated glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation.
source: Furthermore, the scRNAseq identified MS023-specific subpopulations to be metabolically altered with upregulated glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation (OxPhos).
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by scRNAseq analysis and Seahorse metabolic assays shown in Figure 4.

claim: Transplantation of MuSCs treated with MS023 had a better ability to repopulate the MuSC niche and contributed efficiently to muscle regeneration following injury.
source: Transplantation of MuSCs treated with MS023 had a better ability to repopulate the MuSC niche and contributed efficiently to muscle regeneration following injury.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by engraftment experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The preclinical mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy had increased grip strength with MS023 treatment.
source: Interestingly, the preclinical mouse model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy had increased grip strength with MS023 treatment.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by grip strength measurements in mdx mice shown in Figure 6.

claim: The number of Pax7+/ki67+ cells increased significantly in the presence of MS023 for 48 hr.
source: The number of Pax7+/ki67+ cells increased significantly in the presence of MS023 (Eram et al., 2016) for 48 hr (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1A and B which shows immunofluorescence and quantification data.

claim: There was a significant increase in the number of clusters with 3 or more cells with MS023 treatment.
source: We observed a significant increase in the number of clusters with 3 or more cells with MS023 treatment (Figure 1B), as observed for PRMT1-deficient MuSCs (Blanc et al., 2017).
evidence: The text states this finding, references Figure 1B for data, and cites a previous study on PRMT1-deficient MuSCs.

claim: Treatment with a specific CARM1 inhibitor TP-064 over the course of 6 days did not increase MuSC cell number.
source: Treatment with a specific CARM1 inhibitor TP-064 (Nakayama et al., 2018) over the course of 6 days did not increase MuSC cell number, ruling out that MS023 increased proliferation was mediated by CARM1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text states this finding, references Figure 1—figure supplement 1A for data, and cites the source of the TP-064 inhibitor.

claim: PRMT1 is by far the most expressed type I PRMT in MuSCs at every time point tested.
source: Their findings show that PRMT1 is by far the most expressed type I PRMT in MuSCs at every time point tested (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text states this finding based on analysis of publicly available scRNAseq data and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: MS023 treatment restricted the proportion of committed Pax7-/MyoD+ cells, while expanding the proportion of activated and cycling cells (Pax7+/MyoD+).
source: Interestingly, MS023 treatment restricted the proportion of committed Pax7-/MyoD+ cells, while expanding the proportion of activated and cycling cells (Pax7+/MyoD+, Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1C and D which shows immunofluorescence and quantification data.

claim: MuSCs spontaneously differentiate into non-cycling myoblasts and lose their stemness in vitro.
source: MuSCs spontaneously differentiate into non-cycling myoblasts and lose their stemness in vitro (Montarras et al., 2005; Ryall et al., 2015; Sacco et al., 2008).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites three previous studies.

claim: MuSCs incubated with MS023 for 48 hr had reduced ADMA containing proteins.
source: MuSCs incubated with MS023 for 48 hr had reduced ADMA containing proteins, as visualized by immunoblotting (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), and had increased proliferative capacity of MuSCs, as determined by ki67 expression by immunofluorescence and FACS analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D and E).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1C which shows western blot data.

claim: MS023 treatment prevented initiation of differentiation, as indicated by the significantly reduced sub-population of committed Pax7-/MyoD+ cells compared to control DMSO culture (13% vs 31%, respectively).
source: Importantly, immunofluorescence analysis of myogenic markers in cultured MuSCs revealed that MS023 treatment prevented initiation of differentiation, as indicated by the significantly reduced sub-population of committed Pax7-/MyoD+ cells compared to control DMSO culture (13% vs 31%, respectively) (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: The text states this finding with specific percentages and references Figure 1E and F for data.

claim: There was an increase in the proportion of cells that have retained their stemness by delaying expression of MyoD (Pax7+/MyoD-) in the MS023-treated samples compared to DMSO (40% vs 9%).
source: Additionally, there was an increase in the proportion of cells that have retained their stemness by delaying expression of MyoD (Pax7+/MyoD-) in the MS023-treated samples compared to DMSO (40% vs 9%, Figure 1E and F).
evidence: The text states this finding with specific percentages and references Figure 1E and F for data.

claim: The impediment of precocious differentiation observed by treatment with MS023 led to enhanced long-term culture capabilities of MuSCs up to the 14th passage.
source: Furthermore, we observed that the impediment of precocious differentiation observed by treatment with MS023 led to enhanced long-term culture capabilities of MuSCs up to the 14th passage (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The text states this finding and references Figure 1—figure supplement 1F for data.

claim: After filtering out low-quality cells, approximately 4000 cells (average, 3,887±44 cells) from each sample were retained for subsequent analysis.
source: After filtering out low-quality cells, approximately 4000 cells (average, 3,887±44 cells) from each sample were retained for subsequent analysis (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The text provides specific cell numbers from the scRNAseq analysis.

claim: A Pearson correlation of >0.98 was obtained between replicates.
source: A Pearson correlation of >0.98 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) was obtained between replicates and we chose to include a replicate for each time point for analysis.
evidence: The text states this statistical measure and references Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Dimensionality reduction was performed using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) on pooled cells from all samples, resulting in 10 distinct subpopulations of myogenic cells.
source: Dimensionality reduction was performed using uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP) on pooled cells from all samples, resulting in 10 distinct subpopulations of myogenic cells (labelled 0–9, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text describes the computational method used and the resulting number of clusters, referencing Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The freshly isolated MuSCs of day 0 (d0) segregated into Q1 and Q2.
source: The freshly isolated MuSCs of day 0 (d0) segregated into Q1 and Q2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, Supplementary file 3), which in addition to Pax7 and Myf5, expressed markers of MuSC quiescence (Fos, Egr1, Jun), and early activation markers (Myod1, Mt1, Mt2, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The text states this finding and references figures and supplementary files for data.

claim: Q1 and Q2 populations are similar to quiescence and early activation populations reported recently from freshly isolated MuSCs.
source: Our Q1 and Q2 populations are similar to quiescence and early activation populations reported recently from freshly isolated (De Micheli et al., 2020; Dell'Orso et al., 2019; van Velthoven et al., 2017).
evidence: The text compares the identified populations to those in previous studies and cites three references.

claim: The control DMSO day 4 (d4) sample was distributed among three subpopulations of myoblasts (M1, M2, and M4).
source: The control DMSO day 4 (d4) sample was distributed among three subpopulations of myoblasts (M1, M2, and M4), while two additional days in culture day 6 (d6) contained M1, M2, and M4, but also had differentiated clusters DM1 and DM2 (Figure 2C and D; Figure 2—figure supplement 1E, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The text describes the distribution of cells across clusters and references figures and supplementary files.

claim: Day 4 with MS023 (d4MS023) was distributed uniquely among clusters M3 and M5.
source: In comparison, day 4 with MS023 (d4MS023) was distributed uniquely among clusters M3 and M5.
evidence: The text describes the unique distribution of MS023-treated cells.

claim: d6MS023rd4 had nearly twice as many cells in DM1 (20.8%) as d6 (11.5%).
source: Notably, d6MS023rd4 had nearly twice as many cells in DM1 (20.8%) as d6 (11.5%; Figure 2D), indicating that the differentiation block induced by MS023 was reversible.
evidence: The text provides specific percentages and references Figure 2D, and draws an inference about reversibility.

claim: The d4MS023-occupied cluster M5 was enriched for cell cycle markers (Cdk1, Cdk4, Ccnd3) and other markers of proliferation (Mki67, Birc5, Top2a).
source: For example, the d4MS023-occupied cluster M5 was enriched for cell cycle markers (Cdk1, Cdk4, Ccnd3) and other markers of proliferation (Mki67, Birc5, Top2a) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The text describes gene enrichment in a specific cluster and references supplementary data.

claim: The other d4MS023-occupied cluster M3 retained some markers of proliferation (Ccnd1), however also expressed the cell cycle inhibitor Cdkn2a and the structural muscle gene Myl6, in addition to a strong enrichment for ribosomal genes.
source: The other d4MS023-occupied cluster M3 retained some markers of proliferation (Ccnd1), however also expressed the cell cycle inhibitor Cdkn2a and the structural muscle gene Myl6, in addition to a strong enrichment for ribosomal genes (over 20% of the top 100 markers belonged to the ribosomal protein family, a feature that is unique to cluster M3).
evidence: The text describes the gene expression profile of cluster M3 with specific genes and percentages.

claim: d4MS023 genes were strongly enriched for the Reactome Pathway of respiratory electron transport, the citric acid cycle, and formation of ATP.
source: Interestingly, d4MS023 genes were strongly enriched for the Reactome Pathway of respiratory electron transport, the citric acid cycle, and formation of ATP.
evidence: The text describes pathway enrichment analysis results.

claim: d4 was enriched for the Reactome Pathways of RNA metabolism, translation, and mRNA splicing.
source: In contrast, d4 was enriched for the Reactome Pathways of RNA metabolism, translation, and mRNA splicing (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: The text describes pathway enrichment analysis results and references figures.

claim: With MS023 treatment, three subpopulations emerged, a Pax7 negative (expression level 0) and two Pax7-positive cell (standard distribution around expression level 1) populations.
source: Meanwhile, with MS023 treatment, three subpopulations emerged, a Pax7 negative (expression level 0) and two Pax7-positive cell (standard distribution around expression level 1) populations.
evidence: The text describes the distribution of Pax7 expression in MS023-treated cells.

claim: The Pax7-positive cell populations in d4MS023 and d4MS023rd4 had higher Pax7 expression levels than their untreated counterparts and were more comparable with day 0 (quiescent) MuSC Pax7 expression levels.
source: The Pax7-positive cell populations in d4MS023 and d4MS023rd4 had higher Pax7 expression levels than their untreated counterparts and were more comparable with day 0 (quiescent) MuSC Pax7 expression levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The text compares Pax7 expression levels across conditions and references a figure.

claim: The trajectory analysis of all samples pooled produced a pseudotime axis with a single branchpoint and 3-cell states which we labelled Q for quiescence, M for myoblast, and DM for differentiating myoblast.
source: The trajectory analysis of all samples pooled produced a pseudotime axis with a single branchpoint and 3-cell states which we labelled Q for quiescence, M for myoblast, and DM for differentiating myoblast (Figure 3A).
evidence: The text describes the results of trajectory analysis and references Figure 3A.

claim: d4MS023 and d6MS023rd4 cells emerge later along the pseudotime axis than d4 and d6 cells and appeared closer to the branchpoint.
source: Interestingly, d4MS023 and d6MS023rd4 cells emerge later along the pseudotime axis than d4 and d6 cells and appeared closer to the branchpoint (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes the positioning of cells in pseudotime and references a figure.

claim: Genes involved in the myogenic process were highly upregulated along the branch that diverges upwards along the trajectory (e.g. Tnnt1, Tnnt2, Acta1, Myog).
source: As expected, genes involved in the myogenic process were highly upregulated along the branch that diverges upwards along the trajectory (e.g. Tnnt1, Tnnt2, Acta1, Myog), while genes involved in cell cycle and proliferation were upregulated along the branch that diverges downwards along the trajectory (e.g. Mki67, Cdca8, Top2a, Birc5) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The text describes gene expression patterns along trajectory branches and references figures.

claim: The DMSO trajectory had 1517 unique genes, while the MS023 trajectory had 2037 unique genes.
source: The DMSO trajectory had 1517 unique genes, while the MS023 trajectory had 2037 unique genes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The text provides specific numbers of unique genes and references a figure.

claim: The MS023 trajectory-unique genes revealed an enrichment for oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis.
source: Interestingly, the MS023 trajectory-unique genes revealed an enrichment for oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial ATP synthesis (Figure 3F and G), consistent with cluster marker analysis for MS023-specific clusters ((Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D): electron transport, ATP synthesis).
evidence: The text describes pathway enrichment results and references multiple figures.

claim: Expression of select genes involved in the mitochondrial electron transport chain (Ndua2, Ndufa4, Uqcr10, Cox4I1, Cox5b, Cox8a, Atp5c1, AtpIf1, Atp5j2) were elevated in MS023-specific clusters.
source: Expression of select genes involved in the mitochondrial electron transport chain (Ndua2, Ndufa4, Uqcr10, Cox4I1, Cox5b, Cox8a, Atp5c1, AtpIf1, Atp5j2) were further examined for expression level within the scRNAseq UMAP plot, and it was confirmed that they were elevated in MS023-specific clusters (Figure 4A).
evidence: The text describes gene expression analysis and references Figure 4A.

claim: RT-qPCR analysis of a subset of these genes confirmed they were upregulated in d4MS023 MuSCs compared to d4 MuSCs.
source: Moreover, RT-qPCR analysis of a subset of these genes confirmed they were upregulated in d4MS023 MuSCs compared to d4 MuSCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes RT-qPCR validation and references a figure.

claim: MS023-treated MuSCs displayed increased OCR measurements at nearly all timepoints (p=0.000001–0.02), with significantly elevated basal respiration (p=0.006) and maximal respiration (p=0.04).
source: As predicted, MS023-treated MuSCs displayed increased OCR measurements at nearly all timepoints (Figure 4B, p=0.000001–0.02), with significantly elevated basal respiration (p=0.006) and maximal respiration (p=0.04), and a trend of increased ATP production (approaching statistical significance, p=0.1).
evidence: The text provides specific statistical values from Seahorse analysis and references Figure 4B.

claim: The average intensity of the MitoTracker signal was significantly increased in d4MS023 cells (p<0.0001).
source: The average intensity of the MitoTracker signal was significantly increased in d4MS023 cells (Figure 4C and D, p<0.0001).
evidence: The text provides a specific p-value and references figures showing MitoTracker staining data.

claim: Several of the marker genes for MS023-specific clusters were components of glycolysis which displayed increased expression compared to clusters of DMSO-treated cells (Hk1, Eno1, Pfkm, Gapdh, Pkm, Slc2a1).
source: Indeed, several of the marker genes for MS023-specific clusters were components of glycolysis which displayed increased expression compared to clusters of DMSO-treated cells (Hk1, Eno1, Pfkm, Gapdh, Pkm, Slc2a1; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text describes gene expression patterns and references a figure.

claim: MS023-treated cells were strikingly more glycolytic than DMSO-treated cells, with glycolysis, glycolytic capacity, and glycolytic reserve all significantly increased (p=0.02, p=0.004 and p=0.001, respectively).
source: MS023-treated cells were strikingly more glycolytic than DMSO-treated cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C). Glycolysis, glycolytic capacity, and glycolytic reserve were all significantly increased (p=0.02, p=0.004 and p=0.001, respectively) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text provides specific p-values from ECAR analysis and references a figure.

claim: d4MS023 cells had significantly higher levels of glucose uptake (measured as grams/liter per 10,000 cells, p=0.004).
source: As expected, d4MS023 cells had significantly higher levels of glucose uptake (measured as grams/liter per 10,000 cells, p=0.004).
evidence: The text provides a specific p-value from glucose uptake measurements.

claim: The glycolytic byproduct lactate was present in higher concentrations d4MS023 media and was undetectable in the d4 media.
source: Additionally, the glycolytic byproduct lactate was present in higher concentrations d4MS023 media and was undetectable in the d4 media (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The text describes lactate measurements and references a figure.

claim: Cells differentiated in the presence of MS023 had an impaired ability to form multinucleated myotubes and had a poor fusion index of 19% compared to the 77% fusion index observed with DMSO treated MuSCs.
source: Expectedly, cells differentiated in the presence of MS023 had an impaired ability to form multinucleated myotubes and had a poor fusion index of 19% compared to the 77% fusion index observed with DMSO treated MuSCs (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The text provides specific fusion index percentages and references figures.

claim: MS023wo cells had completely restored their ability to terminate differentiation, with their fusion index of 76% being comparable to that of DMSOwo cells (78%).
source: Interestingly, MS023wo cells had completely restored their ability to terminate differentiation, with their fusion index of 76% being comparable to that of DMSOwo cells (78%) (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: The text provides specific fusion index percentages and references figures.

claim: The mice that received MS023-treated MuSCs had more GFP+ mature muscle fibers than the mice that received DMSO-treated MuSCs (88 fibers/section ±32 for MS023 versus 31 fibers/section ±14 for DMSO, p=0.02).
source: Interestingly, the mice that received MS023-treated MuSCs had more GFP+ mature muscle fibers than the mice that received DMSO-treated MuSCs (88 fibers/section ±32 for MS023 versus 31 fibers/section ±14 for DMSO, p=0.02; Figure 5E and F).
evidence: The text provides specific fiber counts with standard deviations and p-value, and references figures.

claim: MS023-treated MuSC engraftment yielded an ~7-fold increase in the number of GFP+ following muscle regeneration (p=0.004).
source: Strikingly, MS023-treated MuSC engraftment yielded an ~7-fold increase in the number of GFP+ following muscle regeneration (p=0.004; Figure 5G and H).
evidence: The text provides a specific fold-change and p-value, and references figures.

claim: Reduced ADMA proteins and a subsequent increase in SDMA proteins were observed in MS023-treated mdx mice compared to vehicle-treated mdx mice.
source: We observed reduced ADMA proteins and a subsequent increase in SDMA proteins in MS023-treated mdx mice compared to vehicle-treated mdx mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes western blot results and references a figure.

claim: A 50% increase in 2-paw grip strength (p=0.0113) and a 45% increase (p=0.0089) in 4-paw grip strength were observed in the MS023-treated mice versus those that received vehicle at the 10-day time point.
source: We observed a 50% increase in 2-paw grip strength (p=0.0113) and a 45% increase (p=0.0089) in 4-paw grip strength in the MS023-treated mice versus those that received vehicle at the 10-day time point (Figure 6B).
evidence: The text provides specific percentage increases and p-values, and references Figure 6B.

claim: MS023-treated mice responded with a~30% increase in force compared to their vehicle-treated counterparts (p=0.00727).
source: Interestingly, this experiment revealed that MS023-treated mice responded with a~30% increase in force compared to their vehicle-treated counterparts (p=0.00727; Figure 6C).
evidence: The text provides a specific percentage increase and p-value from force/frequency measurements, and references Figure 6C.

claim: A reduction in the variation of the minimum Feret diameter measurements of fibers from TA cross-sections of MS023-treated mice was observed (p=0.04).
source: Moreover, we observed a reduction in the variation of the minimum Feret diameter measurements of fibers from TA cross-sections of MS023-treated mice (p=0.04; Figure 6D and E).
evidence: The text provides a specific p-value and references figures showing histological analysis.

claim: MuSCs reside on the periphery of muscle fibers in skeletal muscle and are activated following injury to drive muscle regeneration.
source: Muscle stem cells (MuSCs) reside on the periphery of muscle fibers in skeletal muscle and are activated following injury to drive muscle regeneration (Lepper et al., 2011; Relaix and Zammit, 2012).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: Purified MuSCs spontaneously differentiate upon ex vivo expansion.
source: Purified MuSCs spontaneously differentiate upon ex vivo expansion (Fu et al., 2015a; Sacco et al., 2008), limiting the potential of CRISPR Cas9-based applications and stem cell engraftment therapy.
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: Ex vivo cultured MuSCs are vastly inferior at engrafting and contributing to muscle regeneration compared to freshly isolated MuSCs.
source: It is known that ex vivo cultured MuSCs are vastly inferior at engrafting and contributing to muscle regeneration compared to freshly isolated MuSCs, indicating the importance of retaining stemness for MuSC engraftment and muscle regeneration (Montarras et al., 2005; Sakai et al., 2017).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: Cell-intrinsic defects in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) prevent MuSCs from maintaining a proper balance between stem cell self-renewal and differentiation, ultimately leading to depletion of regeneration-competent MuSCs.
source: Cell-intrinsic defects in patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) prevent MuSCs from maintaining a proper balance between stem cell self-renewal and differentiation, ultimately leading to depletion of regeneration-competent MuSCs (Bentzinger et al., 2014; Dumont et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge about DMD and cites three references.

claim: Quiescent MuSCs predominantly rely on fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and oxidative phosphorylation (OxPhos).
source: Quiescent MuSCs predominantly rely on fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and oxidative phosphorylation (OxPhos; Machado et al., 2017; Ryall et al., 2015).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: Glycolysis is upregulated as MuSCs begin to proliferate following activation, representing a metabolic shift in activated MuSCs.
source: While glycolysis remains low in quiescent cells, it is upregulated as MuSCs begin to proliferate following activation, representing a metabolic shift in activated MuSCs (L'honoré et al., 2018; Ryall et al., 2015).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: PRMT1-null mouse MuSCs are highly proliferative and can be expanded in culture, but are unable to terminate differentiation, leading to a severe muscle regeneration defect in vivo following muscle injury.
source: PRMT1-null mouse MuSCs are highly proliferative and can be expanded in culture, but are unable to terminate differentiation, leading to a severe muscle regeneration defect in vivo following muscle injury (Blanc et al., 2017).
evidence: The text describes previous findings about PRMT1-null MuSCs and cites a reference.

claim: CARM1 methylates the myogenic transcription factor, PAX7, to complex with histone methyltransferase complex to allow the expression of myogenic transcription factor Myf5 during asymmetric stem cell divisions.
source: CARM1 methylates the myogenic transcription factor, PAX7, to complex with histone methyltransferase complex to allow the expression of myogenic transcription factor Myf5 during asymmetric stem cell divisions (Kawabe et al., 2012).
evidence: The text describes a specific molecular mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: CARM1 regulates MuSCs metabolism by methylating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) in MuSCs.
source: CARM1 regulates MuSCs metabolism by methylating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) in MuSCs (Stouth et al., 2020).
evidence: The text describes a specific regulatory mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: PRMT5 regulates MuSC proliferation by epigenetically downregulating expression of the cell cycle inhibitor p21 and deletion of PRMT5 in MuSCs blocks their expansion ex vivo and causes defects in muscle regeneration in vivo.
source: PRMT5 regulates MuSC proliferation by epigenetically downregulating expression of the cell cycle inhibitor p21 and deletion of PRMT5 in MuSCs blocks their expansion ex vivo and causes defects in muscle regeneration in vivo (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: The text describes the role of PRMT5 in MuSCs and cites a reference.

claim: PRMT7 functions in the myogenic process and is required for MuSC self-renewal and muscle regeneration, as deletion of PRMT7 in MuSCs leads to persistent p21 expression.
source: PRMT7 functions in the myogenic process and is required for MuSC self-renewal and muscle regeneration, as deletion of PRMT7 in MuSCs leads to persistent p21 expression (Blanc et al., 2016).
evidence: The text describes the role of PRMT7 in MuSCs and cites a reference.

claim: An inhibitor of Setd7-mediated lysine methylation was shown to have beneficial effects on self-renewal and regeneration.
source: Indeed, an inhibitor of Setd7-mediated lysine methylation (Judson et al., 2018), was shown to have beneficial effects on self-renewal and regeneration.
evidence: The text describes previous findings about a Setd7 inhibitor and cites a reference.

claim: The transition from quiescence to proliferation is regulated by a shift from OxPhos to glycolysis.
source: The transition from quiescence to proliferation is regulated by a shift from OxPhos to glycolysis (Pala et al., 2018; Ryall et al., 2015).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: During MuSC quiescence, high levels of NAD+ are generated by oxidative metabolism which in turn activates Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) to deacetylate and repress expression of differentiation genes required for the myogenic program.
source: During MuSC quiescence, high levels of NAD +are generated by oxidative metabolism which in turn activates Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) to deacetylate and repress expression of differentiation genes required for the myogenic program (Ryall et al., 2015).
evidence: The text describes a specific molecular mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: Entry to the process of terminal differentiation is mediated by the activation of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), marking a switch from glycolysis to OxPhos.
source: Furthermore, it has been shown that entry to the process of terminal differentiation is mediated by the activation of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH), marking a switch from glycolysis to OxPhos (Hori et al., 2019).
evidence: The text describes a specific metabolic switch and cites a reference.

claim: Activated AMPK stimulates autophagy, mitophagy, and mitochondrial biogenesis, thus maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis.
source: Activated AMPK stimulates autophagy, mitophagy, and mitochondrial biogenesis, thus maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis (Herzig and Shaw, 2018).
evidence: The text describes the role of AMPK and cites a reference.

claim: Inhibition of type I PRMTs in MuSCs stimulated the expression of autophagic markers (Atg5, Lamp1, Lamp2, Sqstm1) downstream targets of AMPK.
source: Our data showed that inhibition of type I PRMTs in MuSCs stimulated the expression of autophagic markers (Atg5, Lamp1, Lamp2, Sqstm1) downstream targets of AMPK, however it remains to be determined whether AMPK is involved in MS023-treated cells.
evidence: The text describes gene expression findings from the study data.

claim: PRMT1 has been shown to interact with AMPK in skeletal muscle during the early stages of muscle atrophy.
source: PRMT1 has been shown to interact with AMPK in skeletal muscle during the early stages of muscle atrophy (Stouth et al., 2018).
evidence: The text describes a previous finding and cites a reference.

claim: CARM1 directly methylates AMPK to regulate its activity during muscle response to denervation.
source: Moreover, CARM1 directly methylates AMPK to regulate its activity during muscle response to denervation (Stouth et al., 2020).
evidence: The text describes a specific molecular mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: PRMT1 acts through the transcriptional co-activator PGC-1α in human and mouse adipocytes to regulate thermogenic fat activation, and PRMT1-deficient mice were unable to induce the thermogenic program following cold exposure.
source: PRMT1 acts through the transcriptional co-activator PGC-1αin human and mouse adipocytes to regulate thermogenic fat activation, and PRMT1-deficient mice were unable to induce the thermogenic program following cold exposure (Qiao et al., 2019).
evidence: The text describes a specific regulatory mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: Methylation of PGC-1α by PRMT1 was shown to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and may regulate nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes.
source: Methylation of PGC-1αby PRMT1 was also shown to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis and may regulate nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes (Teyssier et al., 2005).
evidence: The text describes a specific molecular mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: PRMT1-mediated methylation positively regulates the insulin receptor (IR)-phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3-K) pathway which is required for glucose transport in skeletal muscle.
source: Additionally, PRMT1-mediated methylation positively regulates the insulin receptor (IR)-phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3-K) pathway which is required for glucose transport in skeletal muscle (Iwasaki and Yada, 2007).
evidence: The text describes a specific regulatory mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: Overexpression of PRMT1 in the liver under hypoxic conditions causes hypermethylation of FoxO1 and increased translocation to the nucleus, resulting in reduced glucose uptake.
source: Overexpression of PRMT1 in the liver under hypoxic conditions causes hypermethylation of FoxO1 and increased translocation to the nucleus, resulting in reduced glucose uptake (Bayen et al., 2018).
evidence: The text describes a specific molecular mechanism and cites a reference.

claim: MS023 has been shown to inhibit several type I PRMTs at nanomolar (nM) concentrations.
source: In vitro, MS023 has been shown to inhibit several type I PRMTs at nanomolar (nM) concentrations (Eram et al., 2016).
evidence: The text describes the properties of MS023 and cites a reference.

claim: PRMT1 is the major cellular type I enzyme.
source: It is well-documented that PRMT1 is the major cellular type I enzyme (Pawlak et al., 2000) and this is why PRMT1, but not the other type I PRMTs are embryonic lethal in mice (Guccione and Richard, 2019).
evidence: The text states this as established knowledge and cites two references.

claim: The numerous published data in cellulo with MS023 are thus far only reproduced by PRMT1-deficiency by siRNA or knockout, suggesting that MS023 actions in vivo are predominantly mediated by inhibiting PRMT1.
source: The numerous published data in cellulo with MS023 are thus far only reproduced by PRMT1-deficiency by siRNA or knockout, suggesting that MS023 actions in vivo are predominantly mediated by inhibiting PRMT1 (Gao et al., 2019; Plotnikov et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2019).
